label: More Single View Geometry
notes: Welcome the class to the single-view chapter spanning printed pages 195 through 236. The thesis is that one perspective image is a projective measuring device: planes become homographies, directions become vanishing points, and the image of the absolute conic stores the internal calibration we want to recover from a single photograph.

label: Camera Center: Homography vs Parallax
notes: Stress that a fixed camera center makes every change a pure rotation, so points along one ray stay coincident and the induced map is the conjugacy K R K-inverse. The moment the center translates, near and far points split into parallax, which is the first depth signal in any image sequence we encounter.

label: Vanishing Points and the Horizon
notes: Define a vanishing point as the image of a scene direction, v equals K R d. Emphasise that all parallel lines of one family converge to that single point, and the vanishing line of a plane collects the vanishing points of every direction lying in the plane, giving the horizon for the ground.

label: The Image of the Absolute Conic
notes: Introduce omega as the calibration written as a conic, equal to K-inverse-transpose times K-inverse. It depends only on the intrinsics, never on rotation, so it is the bridge between pixel algebra and ray angles. Cholesky of its inverse returns K, which is why omega is the calibration target.

label: Angles from Image Points
notes: Show that omega turns dot products of rays into a measurable form, so the cosine of the angle between two image points uses omega in numerator and denominator. The key corollary: orthogonal directions force v-i transpose omega v-j equal to zero, a single linear constraint per orthogonal pair.

label: Calibration from Orthogonal Vanishing Points
notes: Walk through the calibration pipeline: each orthogonal vanishing-point pair gives one linear equation in the entries of omega. With square pixels three mutually orthogonal vanishing points suffice; stack the constraints, solve the nullspace by SVD, then Cholesky-factor to read focal length and principal point.

label: Rotation Invariance of Omega
notes: Reinforce the symbolic check from the notebook: replacing K by K R inside the IAC formula leaves omega unchanged because the rotation cancels with its inverse transpose. Calibration therefore does not require knowing camera orientation, which is what makes vanishing-point calibration practical from a single uncontrolled photo.

label: Metric Plane and the Calibrating Conic
notes: Connect omega to a visible object. The calibrating conic K-inverse-transpose diag one one minus one K-inverse is a real conic in the image whose centre and shape encode the same intrinsics omega stores algebraically. A metric plane with known angles supplies extra constraints when fewer orthogonal directions are available.

label: Single-View Height Transfer
notes: Explain Criminisi-style metrology: with the ground vanishing line and the vertical vanishing point, a known reference height transfers along the vertical homology to any other upright segment. The construction is pure projective incidence, requiring no camera pose, only the horizon and the vertical direction's image.

label: Reading the Affine Ratio
notes: Make the measurement concrete: after transferring the reference, rectify the imaged vertical line by sending the vertical vanishing point to infinity. Once at infinity the cross-ratio collapses to an affine ratio, and the recovered height ratio in the notebook matches the synthetic ground truth exactly.

label: Conics, Quadrics, and Back-Projection
notes: Generalise from points to outlines. An image conic back-projects to a cone through the centre, and conversely a quadric projects to an apparent contour conic because tangent image lines pull back to tangent planes. The dual relation C-star equals P Q-star P-transpose makes the projection a clean matrix conjugation.

label: Noise, Degeneracy, and Recap
notes: Close with the sensitivity lab and the chapter recap. Linear constraints do not guarantee stability: thin vanishing triangles and short measurement baselines amplify noise sharply. Summarise that omega unifies calibration, angle reading, and metrology, all recoverable from one carefully chosen single view.
